rows.title: Stop/activate/wait races tested
rows.evidence: Iteration 4 (delta F5): SharedLifecycle sync core (single lock owns LifecycleState + three-valued GateEffect; every mutation via LifecycleState::apply; CAS+release one critical section). 5 Loom models exhaust interleavings: two activations -> one winner/one release; activate-vs-stop never both-win-and-release; death-vs-stop one fact; no release after SupervisorLost; duplicate cleanup one winner. Harness detects deliberately weakened CAS (3/5 models fail). Gate: RUSTFLAGS=--cfg nono_loom cargo test -p nono --test loom_lifecycle --release. Iteration 6 (delta F7) added scenario 6, so the R05 model set is complete: 7 Loom models. The two new ones cover the durable store's own race - a recovery reconciling a record while another party confirms the same cleanup (exactly one CleanupConfirmed winner; a recovery that observes the cleanup already proven records nothing) and a recovery racing a stop-then-cleanup (never adopt after cleanup). The recovery's read-decide-record is deliberately not one critical section - reconcile() is pure over an already-read state - and these models are what say that gap is safe.

rows.title: Detached sessions/attach survive caller restart
rows.evidence: Iteration 6 (delta F7) landed slice A: durable schema-versioned session store + identity-reconciled recovery (ADR-0001 s6), library-level in crates/nono/src/lifecycle/session_store.rs. SessionRecord v1 (schema_version const 1; a newer version is typed UnsupportedSchemaVersion found by a version probe read before the rest of the shape, never a field-by-field guess) carrying session UUIDv7, generation, ProcessIdentity, process group, LifecycleState, optional ActivationObservation, created/updated wall timestamps and a bounded opaque metadata copy - no product concept, no command line, no environment. Storage: 0700 dir created-or-opened and CHECKED not repaired (not-a-symlink / owned by the effective uid / no group-or-world bits, each typed); dir opened once O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW and every record reached by openat against that descriptor so no later operation re-walks the path; records <uuid>.json at 0600 (explicit fchmod over the umask), first write O_EXCL, updates write-to-temp + renameat in the same dir (temp O_EXCL, 0600, randomized, not a record name), fsync file then dir. Corruption is typed SessionCorrupt{path,why} and enumeration yields one Result per record, so a corrupt record is reported BESIDE its healthy siblings rather than hiding them. Durable prepare persists at Prepared after the gate-ready observation and every later transition updates the record outside the sync_core lock - the record can lag the live state by one step, which is documented and is exactly why recovery reconciles. Ephemeral PreparedSandbox::prepare is unchanged (no store, no file). Recovery: pure reconcile(state, verdict) -> RecoveryDecision {AlreadyVerified | ProcessGone{basis} | StillRunning{survivors} | Unsettled{reason} | Unsupported{reason}}; a cleanup_verified record is AlreadyVerified whatever the probe says (never adopt a reissued pid); a record in a watched state is moved to Failed with SupervisorLost and persisted. Honest limitation, reported not papered over: a recovered process is NOT our child, so waitpid cannot reach it and its exit code/signal are unobservable - RecoveredSession has no wait, returns no SandboxExit and has no killing Drop; it offers kill_group/kill_pid (same targets<=1 refusal as stop) and verify_cleanup_by(deadline) polling until ESRCH. Generations stay at 1 (one-shot session UUIDs; increments are reserved for slice B's re-prepare). Proven: 27 new unit tests + 2 live, each guard removal-detected (record O_NOFOLLOW dropped -> the symlinked record is followed and the decoy is returned; store-dir O_NOFOLLOW dropped -> the store lands on the link's 0755 target; skip-on-parse-failure -> 4 records become 1; schema check deleted -> a v2 record is read as v1; permission check deleted -> a 0755 store is accepted). Live end-to-end: durable prepare -> a caller that crashes (test-only abandon: gate closed, no kill, no reap) -> fresh SessionStore::open -> the record still says 'prepared' -> recover reconciles it to ProcessGone{PidAbsent} -> verify_cleanup ConfirmedAbsent -> the record reads cleanup_verified. Pending for slice B: detached supervisor that keeps exit facts observable across a restart, attach, and the re-prepare flow that increments generation. Linux verification still blocked (R07).

rows.title: Cleanup verification generation/PID-reuse safe
rows.evidence: Iteration 5 (delta F6): typed CleanupVerification landed (ConfirmedAbsent{basis}/StillPresent{survivors}/Indeterminate{reason}/Unsupported{reason}, closed enum, typed evidence payloads; a sent signal is never a basis). Child leads its own process group (setpgid(0,0) in the trusted pre-exec sequence; failure = typed PreExecStage::ProcessGroup), so a reaped run probes kill(-pgid,0) and an unobserved death probes pid+start_time+boot_id. PID-reuse safe: alive-but-different start time => ConfirmedAbsent{IdentityMismatch}; boot change => ConfirmedAbsent{BootIdChanged} (checked before any probe); unreadable start time => Indeterminate, never a proof of absence; targets <= 1 refused before the syscall. Only ConfirmedAbsent records CleanupConfirmed; duplicate verification refused by the state machine. ActivatedSandbox::stop kills the group (and the child pid, for a setsid escapee) and reports the waitpid observation; StopError::SignalFailed is typed. Live-proven on macOS: verify-after-exit, honest StillPresent for a backgrounded grandchild then ConfirmedAbsent after the consumer kills the group, stop()-then-verify, stopped-before-activation verify; removing setpgid makes the survivor test report ConfirmedAbsent while /bin/sleep 30 still runs. 17 unit + 5 live tests. Iteration 6 (F7) added recovered-session verification: RecoveredSession::verify_cleanup reuses the same verdict machinery over the recorded identity/pgid (DeathObservation::NotReaped, because a recovered process was never waited for by anyone here) and only ConfirmedAbsent marks the record CleanupVerified; ActivatedSandbox::drop now kills the process GROUP before the pid, closing the F6 residual. Pending: Linux verification (R07 blocker); documented dark spot - a descendant that calls setsid leaves the group (needs a cgroup-class mechanism).

rows.title: Machine-readable support report
rows.evidence: Iteration 7 (delta F8) landed lifecycle/support.rs. SupportReport::gather() is infallible and returns a tree of Capability<T> = {status: available|partial|unavailable|unknown, determination: probed_live|platform_api|declared, reason: typed (probed | probe_refused | other_platform | platform_api_linked | not_implemented | not_observable_without_irreversible_change | platform_cannot_express), facts: typed or absent}. NO BARE BOOLEAN anywhere in the serialized tree, locked structurally by a test that walks serde_json::Value and rejects Value::Bool at any depth (removal-detected: adding one bool to CleanupFacts fails 3 tests and prints the JSON pointer). Fields: host (compiled target AND uname(2) sysname/release/version/machine; node name deliberately not read - a hostname is not a capability fact), landlock (REUSES upstream Sandbox::detect_abi + DetectedAbi::has_* for a per-right table filesystem_base/refer/truncate/execute/tcp_network/ioctl_dev/scoping - available only if every right is, else partial; zero diff to sandbox/*), seccomp (upstream's own fork-isolated probe_seccomp_block_network_support -> probed_live), seccomp_user_notification (honestly UNKNOWN: SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_NEW_LISTENER cannot be established without installing a filter that cannot be removed from the installing process, and a kernel release number is not proof since CONFIG_SECCOMP_FILTER can be off), seatbelt (PLATFORM_API not probed_live, with the rationale in reason.why_not_probed: sandbox_init is linked so presence is a compile-time fact, but it applies process-wide and irreversibly, so a live probe must fork - the CLI's setup --check-only does exactly that and is not library machinery; asserted by a macOS test), network_filtering (per-mechanism table incl. seatbelt_per_port_tcp = unavailable/platform_cannot_express naming NetworkFilterUnsupported, so the absence is STATED not inferred), pty (live posix_openpt(O_RDWR|O_NOCTTY) closed immediately -> probed_live) kept SEPARATE from interactive_session (not_implemented) so 'pty: available' cannot be misread as 'the lifecycle will give you one', detached_supervisor + attach (unavailable/not_implemented{R09 slice B} - honest, slice B pending), process_identity (captures THIS process and re-checks: start_time/boot_id/self_recognition all probed_live true on this host), cleanup_verification (signal-0 probes of self and own group, reusing cleanup::{probe_pid,probe_group} made pub(crate) so the report cannot drift from the mechanism), event_observation (per-family fidelity map; kernel_denial = NOT_OBSERVED on BOTH platforms - the lifecycle installs no seccomp-notify listener and macOS Seatbelt denials reach userspace only via the system log; the CLI's log-stream reconstruction is explicitly NOT claimed), dark_spots (typed list of the 4 limits already recorded in module docs: setsid group escape, pgid reuse after reap, exec-or-killed EOF ambiguity, Instant-frozen gate expiry - each with consequence + the file that documents it). Upstream SupportInfo{is_supported} untouched. 17 unit tests + docs/lifecycle/support-report-v1.md with a golden example locked by a snapshot test that reads the doc itself. macOS values live-verified; the Linux halves (landlock ABI table, seccomp probe) are written-unverified behind the R07 Docker blocker.
rows.note: Linux verification BLOCKED pending Docker (see R07). The Linux-only code in support.rs is gather_landlock/gather_seccomp/gather_seccomp_user_notification and the Linux arm of gather_network_filtering; none of it has been executed on a Linux kernel by this stream.

rows.title: Generic event delivery for directly observed events
rows.evidence: Iteration 7 (delta F8) expanded lifecycle/events.rs to the contract shape. LifecycleEvent is now an envelope {session_id: Option<Uuid> (always Some in practice), generation, seq: u64, observed_at: SystemTime captured AT observation, identity: Option<ProcessIdentity>, observation: Observation} around a closed what: LifecycleEventKind {StateChanged (kept, so existing consumers keep their fact), PrepareStarted, SandboxApplied, GateReady, ActivationAttempted{outcome}, Released, ExecObserved, ChildExited{outcome}, StopRequested, StopObserved{outcome}, GateAborted, SupervisorFailure{stage,errno}, CleanupVerdict{verdict}, RecordPersisted{schema_version}}. seq is owned by a crate-internal EventEmitter shared by Arc across the prepared->activated handoff, so one run is ONE unbroken sequence (removal-detected: a second emitter restarts at 0 mid-run and fails both live sequence tests); seq is documented as the ordering authority and observed_at explicitly is NOT (a wall clock can step). ActivationOutcome = {Accepted, RefusedWrongSession, RefusedWrongGeneration, RefusedGateClosed{state}, RefusedExpired, RefusedInvalidToken} carries NO token material by construction, locked by a test that walks the serialized tree rejecting any key named token/nonce/secret/digest and ANY array (every secret in the module is a [u8; N]) plus a long-blob check over serde and Debug (removal-detected). No synthesized kernel denials: the vocabulary has no variant for what the platform does not show. Emission points: prepare() -> PrepareStarted (pre-fork, the one event with no identity); the child's gate-ready record -> SandboxApplied + GateReady; activate() -> ActivationAttempted at every outcome, Released after the claim's write, ExecObserved on EOF; wait() -> ChildExited; stop paths -> StopRequested/StopObserved; abort_gate -> GateAborted (only when a live gate was closed); fail_activation -> SupervisorFailure; verify_cleanup -> CleanupVerdict for EVERY verdict, not only ConfirmedAbsent; SessionStore write -> RecordPersisted (never for a write that failed). Every emit is outside the SharedLifecycle lock and after the fact; SessionHandle::persist was restructured to release the record mutex BEFORE calling the sink, so consumer code never runs under a library lock. Rule the order follows: the fact first, then the state change it caused. Proven: 8 new unit tests + 3 live (whole-vocabulary happy run, stopped run reported as stop_requested/stop_observed rather than child_exited, refused activation carrying no token material), each live test asserting the exact sequence, seq gaplessness, observed_at non-decreasing, and identity present on every event after the fork. docs/lifecycle/lifecycle-event-v1.md carries the field table and a golden example locked by a snapshot test. macOS live-verified; the Linux halves are the same code paths behind the R07 blocker.
rows.note: API shape change for consumers: LifecycleEvent went from enum to struct. LifecycleEvent::StateChanged{from,to,observation} is now LifecycleEventKind::StateChanged{from,to} reached via event.what(), with observation on the envelope. Recorded in HANDOFF.md.
